or_left_corner_wall.blurb: Left Corner Wall is the leftmost section of the Madrone Wall cliff band east of Portland, set beyond the Main Wall and the 4th Class Wall. It holds ten routes, mostly trad corners and cracks with two sport lines mixed in. Difficulty centres on 5.10, with one climb at 5.9, a couple of 5.11s and a single 5.12, so it suits leaders already comfortable placing gear on moderate-to-hard terrain rather than beginners. This end of the cliff stays damp and mossy, so expect green rock and slow drying between rains. A rope long enough for the longest lines in the park will cover everything here.

or_1_parched_cat_cliff_aka_cox_rocks.blurb: Parched Cat Cliff, also called Cox Rocks, is a small basalt wall in the lower gorge of Smith Rock State Park, on the West Side below the main column cliffs. It is the first wall you meet when you arrive there. The ten climbs here are almost all trad crack lines, with one sport route, spanning about 5.9 up to the low 5.12s with several in the 5.10 range. Most visitors head for the better-known Wildfire Wall next door, so these cracks are usually quiet. It rewards climbers who like straightforward crack climbing away from the crowds.

or_2_main_area_john_s_slab_tick_boulder.blurb: This is the main boulder cluster at Tick Ranch, along the Tumalo Creek Trail off Skyliners Road west of Bend. Six or seven small-to-medium boulders sit beside the path, each with a few problems, ten in all. Most are easy slabs and short lines from VB to V2, with one harder problem around V4 on John's Slab itself. Shade varies from boulder to boulder, so some stay cool under the trees while others bake in sun. It is a good stop for a quick warm-up session or for mixed-ability groups, with pads set down on the trail.
or_2_main_area_john_s_slab_tick_boulder.approach: Follow the Tumalo Creek Trail west from the cliff band above the parking area. The boulders sit beside the trail, John's Slab first and the more obvious Tick Boulder just beyond it.
